key_findings.finding: Retrobulbar anesthesia is injected into the intraconal compartment, which contains the optic nerve (CN II), oculomotor nerve (CN III), abducens nerve (CN VI), ciliary ganglion, and the nasociliary branch of V1; the ophthalmic regional-anesthesia review specifically lists CN II, III, and VI within the muscle cone. The trochlear nerve (CN IV), although not listed in that particular abstract, is also a motor nerve traversing the orbit and is clinically blocked by a sufficiently diffuse retrobulbar injection, producing extraocular-muscle akinesia.

The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve (V1) is purely sensory: a retrobulbar block can anesthetize its afferent fibers, particularly the nasociliary/ciliary sensory pathway, but V1 has no efferent motor fibers to block. Oculocardiac-reflex anatomy supports the afferent sensory pathway through ciliary nerves and V1.

Therefore, among answer choices, select the option stating involvement of CN II, III, IV, and VI plus the afferent (sensory) fibers of V1, with no efferent fibers of V1. If a choice claims that V1 has efferent fibers, it is anatomically incorrect.
